name: Inbox-first, guided workflow
thesis: ERIS is a hand-off machine: a report passes coordinator -> office chief -> branch chief -> engineer -> reviewer -> office chief, and every persona's real question is 'what is waiting on me and what do I press'. The redesign makes that question the whole product: every role lands on a personal Inbox whose rows are named by place (Route 1 PM 12.3, Monterey) and by the verb that moves them forward; every object page (Incident, Assessment, Technical form) opens with one Next-step banner that states the plain status, who owns it, what happens after the action, and the single primary button; and the five hand-offs (triage, delegate, assign, review, finalize) become short route-backed guided flows (2-3 steps, no defaults, consequence stated, confirmation named) instead of dialogs with unlabeled selects. Record browsing (Incidents, Event Groups, Assessments) and the statewide Map remain, but as secondary destinations reached from the Inbox or a small Records area, scoped by default to the user's district or office. Navigation is capped at four destinations per role and renders as a bottom bar on phones, an icon rail on iPads and a sidebar on desktops, so the page content starts within 120px of the top on every device instead of 700px today. Backend objects and the state machine are untouched; only labels change, and each label maps 1:1 to a code.

principles.name: Inbox first, records second
principles.statement: The home screen for every role is the list of items waiting on that person, grouped 'Needs you now' / 'Waiting on others' / 'Done recently'. Browsing all incidents or assessments is a deliberate secondary act under Records, never the landing page. Nothing ever silently vanishes: an item you acted on moves to 'Done recently' with the outcome ('Accepted - sent to North GeoTech Office').

principles.name: One banner, one button
principles.statement: Every object page opens with a Next-step banner: plain-language status, owner ('Waiting on you' / 'Waiting on Ana Ruiz, Engineer'), one sentence on what happens after the action, and exactly one primary button when the step is yours. All other actions live in a '...' menu. No page ever tells the user to go act somewhere else.

principles.name: Guided hand-offs, not control panels
principles.statement: Triage, delegate, assign engineer, add reviewer, review, finalize and close are route-backed flows of 2-3 steps with labelled choices, no pre-selected answers, consequence text under every option, a confirmation that names the target ('Delegate the Route 1 PM 12.3 assessment to Maria Lopez?'), and a success toast plus an inbox row that records what happened.

principles.name: Place before ids
principles.statement: Every row, banner and title leads with where the site is (District 7 - Los Angeles - Route 101 - PM 12.3) and the incident title; numeric ids (#40, Assessment #12) appear once, muted, at the end. Codes (office NORTH, D07, FIELD_WORKER, PENDING_OFFICE_DELEGATION) never appear; each has exactly one human label defined in a shared status vocabulary.

principles.name: Show what the decision needs, hide the rest
principles.statement: Each screen carries only the data the role needs for its decision at that step: the coordinator sees photos, reporter and road match; the chief sees place, age and the roster; the reviewer sees the whole form read-only. Provenance, raw coordinates, audit history and GIS chrome are one tap away behind 'Details', 'History' or 'Map tools', never on the first screen.

principles.name: Same model on every device, composed per width
principles.statement: Four width classes (compact < 600, medium 600-839, expanded 840-1199, large >= 1200) drive one set of compositions: list-detail becomes drill-in, tables become cards, side panels become bottom sheets, dialogs become full pages, and maps cap at 45vh with a sheet. Navigation destinations are identical on every device; only the container changes (bottom bar, rail, sidebar). Touch targets are 44px on coarse pointers, and there are no nested scroll regions below 840px.

navigation.model: Per-role destination set of at most four items plus an avatar menu (account, appearance, help, sign out). Destinations: Inbox (home for every role), Records (Incidents | Event Groups | Assessments as segments inside one destination; technical forms are reached from their assessment), Map (renamed from Mission Center), and one role-specific fourth item: Terrain (engineers), Admin (Users | Road inventory, admins). Maintenance reporters get 'My reports' as home and 'New report'. Object pages (incident, assessment, technical form) are not destinations; they open from any list with a persistent back control that returns to the exact list position. Guided flows are sub-routes of their object (/assessments/:id/delegate) so they work as pages on phones and as dialogs on desktops. AppShell becomes a React Router layout route so the shell, collapse state and unread counts persist across navigation.
navigation.desktop: Large (>= 1200px): a 240px left sidebar with icon + label + count badge for Inbox, collapsible to a 64px icon rail; the choice persists in UiSettingsContext. Header 56px: ERIS mark (links to Inbox), page title/breadcrumb ('Records / Incidents / Route 1 PM 12.3'), Help button in a fixed slot (WCAG 3.2.6), avatar menu with name and human role title. Content max-width 1440px; list-detail pages use a 400px list and fluid detail. Expanded (840-1199, e.g. iPad landscape and small laptops): the rail is 72px icons-with-labels by default; list-detail still side by side with a 360px list.
navigation.tablet: Medium (600-839px, iPad portrait and half-width Split View): a 72px left icon rail with 11px labels under the icons, count badge on Inbox; single-pane layouts (list OR detail) with drill-in and a sticky back bar; two-column forms collapse to one; supporting map/photo panes become bottom sheets. Expanded landscape iPads behave as small desktops with the rail (see desktop).
navigation.phone: Compact (< 600px): a 56px bottom tab bar (plus safe-area inset) carrying the role's 2-4 destinations with icon + label and the Inbox count badge; header shrinks to 56px with 'ERIS', page title, Help and avatar. Content starts at about 112px from the top (vs 700px today). Tables render as card lists, flows render as full pages with a sticky bottom action bar, maps are 45vh with a 'Expand' control, and object pages stack banner -> facts -> progress -> history. No hamburger anywhere.

navigation.rationale: Judges and users both read navigation as 'what can I do here'. Today's seven-entry sidebar (Workspace, Operations x4, GIS Tools, Administration, Account) presents four plausible homes for 'the status of an incident' and hides the only actionable page behind the vague 'My Work'. Capping at four destinations follows Apple HIG and Material adaptive-navigation guidance (bottom bar under 600px, rail above), avoids the 20%+ discoverability loss NN/g measured for hamburger menus on desktop and tablet, and makes the mental model identical on every device. Putting the three record lists inside one 'Records' destination with segments removes three sidebar entries without removing any capability, and renaming Mission Center to 'Map' answers the coordinator who could not find the map. Terrain stays a destination only for engineers because they are the only persona whose top task begins there; everyone else reaches it from a technical form.

touchAndDensityRules: Every interactive element is at least 24x24 CSS px with 8px spacing everywhere (WCAG 2.5.8) and at least 44x44 px under @media (pointer: coarse); row height 48px on coarse pointers, 40px on fine pointers, 32px compact only on fine pointers via the Density setting.
Minimum text size 12px anywhere and 14px for body/labels; the 9-11px control text in the 3D scene, legends, chips and back buttons is removed.
Main content starts within 120px of the viewport top on phones and tablets (header 56px + title row) - baseline today is 700px.
No nested vertical scroll regions below 840px except inside a map/scene; below 840px lists render fully and long panels become bottom sheets with their own single scroll.
Maps embedded in pages are capped at 45vh on phones and 50vh on tablets with an Expand control; full-height only on the Map and Terrain destinations; one map per phone screen.

Hover-only affordances are forbidden: every tooltip has a visible label or tap-activated popover; link text is underlined or presented as a button; selected states use border + check glyph + aria-pressed/aria-current, never color alone.
Status pills pair text with a fixed color and never look like buttons (light background, dark text, 3:1 non-text contrast); one color per status across list, banner and map.
Sticky action bars carry one primary button (48px on coarse pointers) and never more than two secondary controls; everything else goes in a '...' menu.
Focus-visible rings on all controls; dialogs and sheets trap focus, restore it, close on Escape, and are announced via aria-labelledby; toasts and banners are live regions.
Widths are viewport-based tokens declared once in Tailwind's @theme (sm 480, md 600, lg 840, xl 1200, 2xl 1440); pages never branch on device names or content width.

Screens-tall budget: Inbox <= 1.5 screens before 'Waiting on others'; object pages <= 3 screens on phone; technical form hub <= 2 screens; a section page <= 3 screens. Baseline: submission page 11.1 screens, canvas 532px in a 375px viewport, 120 small tap targets - targets: 0 overflowing elements, 0 tap targets under 44px on coarse pointers.

backendChanges: #1 Single review decision: POST /assessments/{id}/review (APPROVE / REQUEST_REVISION) also updates the linked submission status (SUBMITTED -> APPROVED / returned) and POST /assessments/{id}/submit accepts the submission id so one 'Submit for review' advances both; reason: two parallel state machines produce contradictory screens ('fix it' vs 'waiting for reviewer') and a lost queue item.

#2 Triage commit: either a combined POST /incidents/{id}/triage that accepts the location/Event Group choice, or allow POST /incidents/{id}/location-link to be changed until the disposition is recorded (can_change_association true); reason: the current first save is irreversible before the decision is made.

#3 Personal and office scoping in list endpoints: /assessments?queue=reviewer must return only items where the caller holds an active REVIEWER/APPROVER assignment (admins too, with an explicit all=true flag); /assessments?state=APPROVED scoped by the caller's office for office chiefs; reason: finalize failing with 403 on items shown in the queue and the admin firehose.

#4 Assessment list items embed incident summary fields (title, district, county, route, post_mile, first_observed_at, photo_count) and per-step timestamps/owners already stored (office_delegated_at, engineer_assigned_at, submitted_at, approved_at, finalized_at) plus the latest note; reason: place-first rows and age without N+1 requests.
#5 Assignment option payloads (branch-options, assignment options) include office/branch name and open_assessment_count; reason: chiefs choose by load and location.

#6 Server-side search, district/office/route filters, sort and cursor pagination on /incidents, /event-groups (with total_count) and /assessments, with route normalization ('80' = 'I-80' = '080'); /event-groups/{id} returns assessment_id and assessment_state per incident; reason: remove 500/1000-row client fetches and enable scope presets.

#7 Web upload of submission attachments with a section tag (reuse the mobile attachment endpoint if it is not restricted to mobile clients); reason: photos are part of the form and the web has no way to add them.
#8 Optional: expose actor names on submission workflow events and reporter names on submission summaries; reason: 'User #7' appears in review contexts.
